policies.title: FBI begins separate animal-cruelty reporting
policies.summary: A new reporting category made some cruelty incidents visible, but changing participation prevents simple national comparisons.
policies.changed: FBI added distinct animal-cruelty coding, including neglect, intentional abuse, organized abuse, and sexual abuse.
policies.afterward: Reporting expanded substantially. The BJS series measures general reporting coverage, not the prevalence of cruelty or the number of suffering animals.
policies.attribution: FBI and participating state/local agencies implemented collection beginning under Obama; later administrations maintained and expanded the broader system. This is a measurement contribution, not proven prevention.
policies.unknown: A stable panel of agencies with validated cruelty reporting and animal-level outcomes has not been assembled here.
policies.mechanism: More specific recording could improve detection, allocation of enforcement resources and prevention; those downstream effects require evaluation.
policies.coverage: Incidents known to and reported by participating law-enforcement agencies.
policies.exceptions: Unreported conduct, nonparticipating agencies and lawful practices are outside these counts.
policies.confidenceReason: Start date and coverage are documented; effectiveness is unestablished.

contributors.role: Designed the category and reporting system
Broader justice statistics oversight; no distinct suffering estimate assigned

policies.title: PETS Act: pets in disaster planning
policies.summary: Emergency planning and assistance provisions recognize household pets and service animals.
policies.changed: State/local emergency plans must account for people with pets and service animals; the statute authorizes relevant assistance and facilities.
policies.afterward: FEMA's April 2025 evacuation annex retains this authority in federal operational guidance.
policies.attribution: 109th Congress passed the law; George W. Bush signed it. FEMA, state/local authorities and responders implement it across administrations.
policies.unknown: No disaster-adjusted causal estimate of pet survival, abandonment or reunification was located in this review.
policies.mechanism: Including animals in evacuation and shelter planning could reduce abandonment and allow owners to evacuate earlier.
policies.coverage: Household pets and service animals in covered disaster preparedness and assistance.
policies.exceptions: This is not a blanket requirement that every hotel or shelter admit every animal.
policies.confidenceReason: Enacted text and current operational guidance support the institutional change, not quantified benefits.

gaps.detail: No harmonized animal-outcome panel with defensible treatment and comparison groups was assembled.
gaps.neededData: Facility/animal-level longitudinal outcomes, stable reporting and exposure timing; appropriate comparisons.
